explain: The Code of Ethics states engineers should build their professional reputation on the basis (merit) of their services, avoiding unfair competition; per the answer key the intended answer is 'basis'.

explain: Ethics deals with judging an individual's actions and behavior in society as right or wrong, good or bad.

explain: Engineering ethics specifically represents a system of moral standards applied to the actual practice of engineering.

q: 11. Which of the following do you consider to be ethical as an engineer?
options: To leave a job you just got for another job that is of same pay but a more professionally rewarding one
To make comments on the works of another engineer
To work for a client on the project which you have appraised as infeasible some time ago
To provide you services at a rate considered due to be too low
explain: Choosing a more professionally rewarding job at the same pay is a legitimate, ethical career decision, unlike the other options which involve conflicts of interest or unprofessional conduct.

options: maintain high level of ethical conduct
explain: Engineers are fundamentally bound to uphold professional advancement alongside maintaining high standards of ethical behavior.

q: 17. Which of the following is considered to be unethical?
options: signing plans prepared by an unknown person without thoroughly reviewing those plans.
not charging a free for presenting a speech
reviewing the mark of another engineer without that engineer's consent
providing professional services as a consultant
explain: Reviewing another engineer's work without their consent violates professional courtesy and ethical norms; as per the answer key, this is the unethical action.

q: 18. For the fulfillment of his/her professional duties Engineer should:
options: paramount the health of the public
paramount the safety of the public
explain: Holding paramount public health, safety, and welfare is the foundational rule of all engineering professional practice codes.

q: 19. Engineer shall practice
options: impartial and efficient professional relationship with client, contractor and fellow professional.
explain: Engineers are ethically bound to maintain an impartial and efficient professional relationship with all parties - clients, contractors, and fellow professionals - rather than favoring one side.

q: 20. Engineers shall build their professional reputation on the ..........of their services and shall not compete unfairly with others.
explain: The standard canon states that engineers must build professional standing based on the merit of their service.
